blocks.text: RMS holds a large multilingual speech and text archive. Scaling what the census read in each sampled folder to every listed folder, the estate most likely holds 500,290.3 hours of media: 190,196.8 hours of speech and 341,566.0 hours of music, estimated separately and not an exact split. The ninety-five per cent forecast interval spans 212,923.5 hours, 42.6% of the forecast. Measured bytes are 175.0 TiB. Only 8.5% of the forecast hours rest on files read and judged, and 73.4% sit in buckets the census key cannot read.

The strongest assets are the languages and the text. Kiswahili (38,788.1 speech hours), Gikuyu (32,002.9) and Ekegusii (16,729.3) lead the forecast, and the news archive adds 248,841 live scripts. Value concentrates: one bucket the key cannot read carries 251,976.0 forecast hours, 50.4% of the estate, while the databases are 0.2% of the bytes.

Preparation is work to do, not a reason to wait: object-read access, a restore decision, finishing the samples, checking the model readings and de-identifying product inputs. The first money path is repricing archive tiering, an upper bound of 986.5 USD a month at legacy reference prices, followed by a speech-and-text pilot. Management is asked to decide access first.

blocks.label: How the forecast was built — the donor folders by media kind
blocks.note: 2,000 seeded simulations over 1,334 folder strata. Measured strata: normal draws around the census estimator and its standard error. Forecast strata: in each simulation a donor folder of the same media kind is drawn — every readable bucket is one witness (bucket weight ∝ √ of its files), its folders share that weight by file count, and a Gaussian kernel on log mean file size (σ = 1.0, widened until at least 3 donors carry weight) favours donors whose files look like the target's; hours = bytes × the donor's seconds per megabyte; speech, music and language hours = hours × the donor's shares. Strata are summed in every simulation; est is the median, lo–hi the 2.5th–97.5th percentiles. Intervals carry sampling and between-folder variation, not model error or the chance that refused buckets differ in kind from every readable one.

sections.heading: The decisions, in order

blocks.text: Grant the census key read access on the refused buckets, starting with the largest at 251,976.0 hours. This is the single step that most reduces uncertainty in the 500,290.3-hour forecast.

Next, complete the samples of readable folders and shares and commission human checks on the model readings. Only then reprice tiering and confirm duplicates by hash. Keep pilot approval, preparation funding and destructive execution as separate decisions, each with an owner and an evidence gate.

sections.heading: What to do first, and why

blocks.text: The forecast of 500,290.3 hours rests on donors, with 8.5% of hours directly judged. It assumes refused buckets resemble readable folders of the same media kind and file size; if not, the truth lies outside the interval. Speech, music and language figures are model readings with sampling intervals only.

Savings, file-share duplication, script language, workbench overlap and buyer demand are also unmeasured. Each gap names its closing step: an access grant, human checks, class and demand data, fingerprinting, a text pass, a hash join or buyer review.

sections.heading: What the evidence cannot yet establish

terms.meaning: Space that could be removed or stored more cheaply once the check named beside it has been done. It is not space already freed, and it is not a guaranteed saving — the monthly figures are upper bounds at list prices.
Nothing new has been written to that bucket or table for more than a year, judged by the newest write date we could see. It says nothing about whether anyone still reads it — that was not measured.
terms.term: Cold (not written for over a year)

terms.meaning: Two objects whose size and storage fingerprint (ETag) match inside the same store. For large uploads that fingerprint is not a content hash, so a candidate must be confirmed by hashing before any copy is removed.
Database rows that are identical in every measured column. 'Normalised' duplicates also match after trimming spaces and case.
A row whose worst column shows damage: text cut short, a placeholder such as 'N/A' or 'test', an invalid format, stray whitespace or garbled characters.

Blank values in columns whose name or pattern suggests they should always be filled (for example an identifier or a date). The database may not formally require them; the census flags them so an owner can decide.
A column that is empty on practically every row: schema carried without data.
A sampled value that looks like an email, phone number, national ID or similar. It is a condition of the data, not a judgement about rights — the owner has declared all rights established.
A cheaper storage tier for data that is kept but rarely opened. Retrieval is slower and carries its own fee, which is why the saving is stated as an upper bound.
Where this pack suggests data should live or how it should be tiered. Every destination here is a proposal for the executive to approve; this pack moved and deleted nothing.
Recorded hours multiplied by the share of two-second windows the admitted music detector did not call music. Silence is set aside first.
The share of labelled windows (or transcript passages) where the model's language label matched the folder the recording was filed under. It is a model reading, not a human verification.
Windows where the language model's confidence fell below its threshold, so it gave no language rather than guess.

A calendar date on which a station has at least one news script in the archive, and the distinct hour slots scripted that day. The archive does not carry a script for every hour of every day; the tables show exactly which days and hours it does.
The retained Akki record (census run, GPU job or database reading) that every figure in this pack is traced to. The appendix lists them; the workbook carries the row-level evidence.

What the entire estate most likely holds, found by scaling what the census read in each folder up to that folder's full population and adding every folder together — the part that could not be read included, each one standing in for a readable folder of the same kind and file size.

The estate was added up thousands of times, each time letting every uncertain folder take a different plausible value. The middle result is the forecast; the range that holds 95 % of the results is the forecast interval.

A folder the census read and judged that stands in for a folder it could not read: same media kind, similar file size. Its seconds per megabyte, speech share and language mix are borrowed, so the forecast is only as representative as its donors.

Measured rows come from files actually read and judged, with a sampling interval. Forecast rows are borrowed from donors and carry a wider interval. Every table says which is which; an access grant or a finished sample turns a forecast row into a measured one.

A duration estimate based on available file headers and per-folder extrapolation for unprobed files. Probing is incomplete; some durations themselves use bitrate estimates. This is not an exact count of decoded estate hours.

A sampling-uncertainty range produced by a method intended to cover its target in 95 % of repeated samples under its assumptions. It does not cover model error, failed reads, unmeasured folders or inaccessible content. Whole-folder reads remove sampling error, not measurement or classification error.

The census key can list the bucket but is refused when it tries to read any object. Those files are counted but nothing about their content is estimated. The fix is an access grant on the owner's cloud account, not a change to the census.

The cheapest storage tier. Some buckets allow direct reads of Archive objects for a retrieval fee; others answer 'restore required', and a restore must be ordered and paid for before anything can be read.

Whole-estate Monte Carlo forecast over the retained content-census receipts (cr-bbf71c8d905a, cr-cb0e66bd3e24, cr-cf4eef79995b, cr-f1415e395361): 2,000 seeded simulations over 1,334 folder strata. Measured strata: normal draws around the census estimator and its standard error. Forecast strata: in each simulation a donor folder of the same media kind is drawn — every readable bucket is one witness (bucket weight ∝ √ of its files), its folders share that weight by file count, and a Gaussian kernel on log mean file size (σ = 1.0, widened until at least 3 donors carry weight) favours donors whose files look like the target's; hours = bytes × the donor's seconds per megabyte; speech, music and language hours = hours × the donor's shares. Strata are summed in every simulation; est is the median, lo–hi the 2.5th–97.5th percentiles. Intervals carry sampling and between-folder variation, not model error or the chance that refused buckets differ in kind from every readable one.
